description:
Guy Lafleur was the electrifying engine of the Montreal Canadiens’ high-powered offense in the 1970s, thrilling fans with his speed, flair, and lethal scoring ability. A five-time Stanley Cup champion and two-time Hart Trophy winner, he became the first player in NHL history to record six straight seasons with 50 goals and 100 points. With his flowing hair and smooth stride, Lafleur became a beloved icon in Montreal and a Hockey Hall of Famer. 

Among his many clutch goals, perhaps the most iconic was his game-tying blast in Game 7 of the 1979 Semifinals against the rival Boston Bruins. With the Canadiens on a late power play and trailing by one, Lafleur led the rush up ice, dished the puck forward, then trailed the play to rip a one-timer off a drop pass that beat the goalie and sent the home crowd into a frenzy. Montreal would go on to win the game in overtime on Yvon Lambert’s goal and later defeat the New York Rangers in the Final to claim their fourth straight Stanley Cup.
